conventions.convention: An admitted domain is nonempty, bounded and Lipschitz, with fixed uniform interior cone radius and aperture at every point of its closure. Cone orientations need only exist pointwise.

Fill distance is the supremum over Ω; separation radius is half the minimum pairwise distance and is defined for at least two sites. Conditional positivity is strict on the polynomial moment-null subspace, and unisolvence means independent evaluation-matrix columns.
The forward Fourier transform has exponent −2πix·ξ and the inverse has exponent +2πix·ξ. For ν>0 and a>0, s=ν+d/2 and w(ξ)=A(a²+4π²|ξ|²)^(−s), normalized to integral one.

H^s(Ω) is the restriction quotient of continuous inverse Fourier representatives with whole-space weight (1+|ξ|²)^s. No identification with an intrinsic fractional-domain norm or extension operator is asserted. Inner products are linear in the first variable.

RBF-FD uses exact real arithmetic, distinct polynomially unisolvent sites, strict conditional positivity, and a homogeneous constant-coefficient functional of order t no greater than the polynomial degree. The Taylor estimate retains the actual sum of absolute weights.
Countable Choice is assumed for the spectral integration suppliers; full AC is carried conservatively by the Fourier Hilbert-space and projection branch.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC conservatively for the declared weighted-L² Hilbert dependency. On an admitted domain, fix ν>0, s=ν+d/2 and an integer m>ν. There exist C,h₀>0 depending only on d,s,m and the cone constants such that every finite nonempty X⊂Ω with h_X≤h₀ and every u∈H^s(Ω) vanishing on X satisfy ‖u‖∞≤C h_X^ν ‖u‖H^s(Ω), without separation or mesh-ratio hypotheses.

Under the stated conservative AC assumption, inverse Fourier representatives with finite integral |g|²/w form a Hilbert space whose kernel sections reproduce evaluation and span densely; its norm is equivalent to H^s(R^d), and the Matérn Gram matrix on every finite distinct site list is strictly positive definite.

For an admitted domain and fixed integer m≥1, there are R,B,h₀>0 depending only on d,m,r₀,θ such that, whenever 0<h_X≤h₀, every x∈closure(Ω) admits J distinct sites within Rh_X and real polynomial-reproduction weights with sum of absolute values at most B, where J=dim Π_(m−1). No separation lower bound is assumed.

Under the stated conservative AC assumption, for every s>d/2 each g∈L²_s is integrable, U_g is bounded and continuous, g↦U_g is injective, and the whole-space Fourier Bessel-potential space is a complex Hilbert space with uniformly bounded point evaluations.

For fixed Matérn parameters and N≥2 distinct sites with separation radius 0<q≤1, there is c=c(d,ν,a)>0 such that λ_min(K_X)≥c q^(2ν), λ_max(K_X)≤N, and κ₂(K_X)≤c^(−1)Nq^(−2ν). For N=1, K_X=[1] and κ₂(K_X)=1.

Under Countable Choice, the stated Matérn spectral density is positive and integrable with integral one; its inverse transform is real, even, radial and continuous with k(0)=1, and satisfies the displayed Gaussian-mixture and Bessel formulas.

On distinct sites, strict positive definiteness makes K_X invertible. Strict conditional positive definiteness of order m together with m-unisolvence makes the polynomially augmented matrix invertible, with a unique solution for every right-hand side.
